newsitem.title: USA: US mortgage-backeds buoyant, yield spreads widen.
newsitem.headline: US mortgage-backeds buoyant, yield spreads widen.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backeds traded higher but spreads to Treasuries widened about two basis points late in the session, traders said.

Trading was thin and pass-throughs lagged the Treasury market after the National Association of Purchasing Management Index provided more evidence that inflation remains subdued despite healthy economic growth.
"It's been fairly quiet today and mortgages widened about two ticks on the day," said one Ginnie trader.
He said he saw light buying across the board, with particular interest in discount coupons.
By late afternoon, pass-through prices rose as high as 11/32, while comparable Treasuries were 8/32 to 14/32.
In key coupons, Ginnie Mae 30-year 7.5 percent coupons were up 7/32 at 100-19/32 bid, yielding 95 basis points over the 10-year Treasury note.
Comparable Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac paper were up 7/32 as well, at 100-16/32 and 100-23/32, respectively.
In Treasury trading, the five-year Treasury note was up 8/32 to yield 6.32 percent, and the 10-year Treasury note was up 15/32, yielding 6.44 percent.
